rationale: A is more robust and semantically faithful: it compiles definitions into explicit instructions, snapshots referenced words and built-ins so later redefinitions do not retroactively change existing definitions, and implements signed integer division with truncation toward zero. Its helpers and naming are clear despite modest extra structure. B is concise, but its token-based expansion allows a built-in used in an older definition to be affected by a later user definition of the same name, and its use of Python floor division gives surprising results for negative operands.
